basics.description: **Altiward server.** Creates an Altiward server in your subscription: a container app running Altiward with caddy beside it, Postgres on a private network, a key vault holding the database URL and tokens, and a Log Analytics workspace for the logs. Roughly US$75–100 a month in UK South. You need Owner, or Contributor and Role Based Access Control Administrator, on the resource group: the template grants its identity and you access to the key vault. [What it creates and what to do next](https://github.com/Altiward/altiward/blob/main/deploy/azure/README.md).

options.text: Macs remember the address they enroll with. If you'll use your own domain for this server, add it before you roll out the agent (README.md, "Your own domain"). Postgres isn't offered in every region or subscription type: if the deployment says so, pick another region.

basics.name: namePrefix
basics.label: Name prefix
basics.toolTip: The start of every resource name, and of the console's address.

constraints.validationMessage: 3 to 12 lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter.

basics.name: organisationName
basics.label: Organisation
basics.toolTip: Your organisation's short name. The tokens carry it, and SIEM events name it.

constraints.validationMessage: Up to 40 letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit.

basics.name: consoleAllowedNetworks
basics.label: Networks allowed to open the console
basics.toolTip: Your office's and VPN's public addresses, space separated. Macs report from anywhere whatever this says. 0.0.0.0/0 allows everyone. You can change it later (README.md).

constraints.validationMessage: IPv4 addresses or ranges, such as 203.0.113.0/24, separated by spaces.

basics.name: postgresAdminPassword
basics.toolTip: For the database's admin user, altiward. The server's database URL in the key vault holds it, so you won't need it day to day.

constraints.validationMessage: At least 12 characters, with upper case, lower case and a digit.
